display.purpose: Page-hero H1s only — the single largest statement on a page.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, buttons, nav links, badges — the busiest type role.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: New baseline resting elevation for cards/frames.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: Hover response for cards, frames, interactive grid items.

shadows.name: deep
shadows.purpose: Floating chrome above page content (nav overflow dropdown).

motion.name: interactive-fast
motion.purpose: Button/link color, transform, and border-color transitions on hover/focus.

motion.name: card-lift
motion.purpose: Card/frame transform and box-shadow transition on hover.

motion.name: hero-breathe
motion.purpose: Slow ambient zoom on page-hero background photography (scale 1.06 to 1).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action. Navy fill, white uppercase label, lifts on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary">Become a partner<svg class="ds-btn-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M5 12h14M13 6l6 6-6 6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 50px; padding: 13px 22px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--axp-navy); color: #fff; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .25s ease, background .25s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #263455; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--axp-gold); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; }

components.name: Secondary (Gold) Button
components.description: The one inverted button — dark label on gold fill. Used sparingly for the single most-wanted action on a surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-gold { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 50px; padding: 13px 22px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--axp-gold); color: var(--axp-navy-2); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .25s ease, background .25s ease; } .ds-btn-gold:hover { background: #e2b240; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-gold:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--axp-gold); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action on light surfaces — navy outline, transparent fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 50px; padding: 13px 22px; border: 1px solid var(--axp-navy); border-radius: 3px; background: transparent; color: var(--axp-navy); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .25s ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--axp-gold); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Opportunity Card
components.description: Flat hairline-bordered card with a faint resting shadow that lifts and deepens on hover.
components.html:
Two-Bedroom Starter Home

A clearly-labelled concept illustrating one possible ownership route.
components.css: .ds-card { padding: 28px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(26,35,61,.13); border-radius: 0; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(26,35,61,.05); transition: transform .3s ease, box-shadow .3s ease; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-5px); box-shadow: 0 24px 60px rgba(26,35,61,.09); } .ds-card-title { margin: 0 0 10px; font-family: var(--font-serif); font-weight: 500; font-size: 20px; color: var(--axp-navy); } .ds-card-copy { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.7; color: #656a76; }

components.name: Input Field (dark panel)
components.description: Square-cornered field as used inside dark form panels (e.g. the opportunity interest form).
components.css: .ds-field-panel { padding: 32px; background: var(--axp-navy-2); border-radius: 0; } .ds-field-label { display: block; margin-bottom: 8px; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(255,255,255,.7); } .ds-field-input { width: 100%; padding: 11px 12px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.16); border-radius: 0; background: rgba(255,255,255,.92); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 14px; color: var(--axp-navy); } .ds-field-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--axp-gold); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Header navigation link with a gold underline that slides in from the left on hover/active.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { position: relative; padding: 28px 0 25px; font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; color: #4f5564; text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-nav-link::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 100%; bottom: 0; height: 2px; background: var(--axp-gold); transition: right .25s ease; } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link--active { color: var(--axp-navy); } .ds-nav-link:hover::after, .ds-nav-link--active::after { right: 0; }

components.name: Eyebrow Label
components.description: The small gold uppercase label that introduces nearly every section — the system's primary wayfinding device.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { margin: 0 0 16px; color: var(--axp-gold); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .18em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Circular Gold-Ring Emblem
components.description: The system's one decorative signature — a thin gold-stroke circle with soft glow rings, always bled off the corner of a dark navy surface, never on light backgrounds.
components.css: .ds-ring-surface { position: relative; overflow: hidden; background: var(--axp-navy); min-height: 260px; } .ds-ring { position: absolute; right: -150px; top: -220px; width: 680px; height: 680px; border: 1px solid rgba(212,160,42,.22); border-radius: 50%; box-shadow: 0 0 0 90px rgba(255,255,255,.014), 0 0 0 180px rgba(255,255,255,.012); }

narrative.overview:
AXP's interface reads like a well-kept institutional record: navy and gold, hairline rules, generous margins, and information presented with the quiet confidence of something that has already earned trust rather than something straining to earn it. The system is warm and reassuring rather than corporate-cold — it borrows the precision of a ledger or letterhead, not the sterility of one, because the audience is often making the biggest financial decision of their life and needs to feel guided, not processed.

Density stays low and unhurried: sections breathe at 112px of vertical padding, copy blocks cap around 65-75 characters, and every major section opens with a small gold eyebrow label before its heading — a consistent wayfinding device that lets a visitor scan the page's structure at a glance. Serif display type (Lora) carries the emotional register of the big claims and section headings; a clean geometric sans (Poppins) carries everything functional — body copy, labels, navigation, buttons — so warmth and precision never compete for the same word.

Gold is treated as a signal, not a fill: it marks eyebrows, focus rings, the accent button, and the active-nav underline, but it never becomes a background or a body-text color. Confirmed visual rejection: this is explicitly not a real-estate-listing aesthetic — no bright multi-photo carousels-as-hero, no urgency badges, no saturated CTA gradients. AXP is 'not selling houses,' and the interface should never look like it's trying to.
keyCharacteristics: Navy-and-gold institutional palette, used with restraint (gold is rare by design)
Serif display headlines (Lora) paired with a geometric sans for everything functional (Poppins)
Small gold uppercase eyebrow labels as a structural, repeated wayfinding device
Flat, hairline-bordered surfaces with a hover lift + shadow response, plus a faint resting shadow for depth
Near-square button corners (3px) — precise, not soft — contrasted with fully pill-shaped micro-badges
A recurring circular gold-ring emblem as the system's one decorative signature, always on dark/navy grounds

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Gold never fills a large surface or colors body text — it always marks a small, deliberate point of attention.

rules.name: The One-Voice-Per-Job Rule
rules.body: Lora is exclusively for emotional/display headlines; Poppins is exclusively for everything functional. Never swap them.

rules.name: The Hover-Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth is a response to interaction, not a resting decoration. A card's shadow always deepens and the card always rises -5px on hover — never the reverse, and never a static heavy shadow at rest.

rules.name: The Square-Precision Rule
rules.body: Anything the visitor acts on directly (buttons, menu items) stays close to square (3px). Anything that's a compact status marker goes fully pill-shaped (999px). Nothing sits in between in the marketing vocabulary.

dos: Do treat gold as a rare signal — eyebrows, one button variant, focus rings, nav underline, the ring emblem — never a fill or body-text color (The One Signal Rule).
Do pair Lora exclusively with display/headline roles and Poppins with everything else; never mix them within the same text role.
Do give interactive surfaces a hairline border + faint rest shadow, then a stronger lift + shadow only on hover (The Hover-Lift Rule).
Do open new major sections with a small gold uppercase eyebrow label above the heading — it's the system's primary wayfinding device and visitors will expect it.

Do use the .prototype-note pill pattern (or an equivalent) whenever a surface shows illustrative/placeholder content (e.g. example opportunity listings), so visitors aren't misled into treating concept content as confirmed fact.
donts: Don't round marketing buttons or menu items beyond 3px, and don't leave a badge/chip square — the system has exactly two corner treatments (near-square, full pill), nothing in between.
Don't fill a card, section, or button with gold, and don't set body copy in gold — it must stay a small, deliberate mark.
Don't introduce urgency/hype patterns (countdown badges, saturated gradient CTAs, stacked photo carousels as hero) — confirmed anti-reference: this is explicitly not a real-estate-listing aesthetic.
Don't invent a new headline clamp() range per component; consolidate new section headings onto the canonical headline token instead of adding another slightly-different size.
Don't treat the currently-unused --axp-blue / --axp-green / --axp-orange tokens as available accents without an explicit design decision to adopt them.
